fills.reason: Searched main sources and manifest for external-storage APIs and permissions: no WRITE/MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE permission and no getExternal*/Environment calls; MediaStore is only used as the data URI of an ACTION_PICK gallery intent, and backups/exports go through the Storage Access Framework (ACTION_CREATE_DOCUMENT/OPEN_DOCUMENT_TREE).

Reviewed every SecretKeySpec construction: vault keys come from scrypt/Argon2/PBKDF2 derivation or slot decryption, HOTP keys are the user's OTP secrets, and importer keys are derived from the user-supplied password. The only constant byte arrays are fixed IVs required by third-party import formats (Authy, TOTP Authenticator), not keys.

Most log calls only record file paths and exception types. But when an otpauth URI has a secret and no host, parseUri puts the whole URI (secret included) into the exception message. That exception is logged with Log.i when the URI comes from the clipboard, and with printStackTrace when it comes from a deep link, so the TOTP secret can end up in logcat.

evidence.detail: Exception message embeds the full otpauth URI, including the secret query parameter.
evidence.quote: String.format("Host not present in URI: %s", uri.toString())

evidence.detail: Clipboard parse failure is logged together with the exception, whose message can contain the secret.
evidence.quote: Log.i("EntryActivity", "Clipboard did not contain a valid otpauth URI", e);

evidence.detail: Deep link parse failure prints the stack trace (with the URI-bearing message) to logcat.

fills.reason: The only WebView (SimpleWebViewDialog, used for changelog and licences) loads bundled HTML with loadData and never calls setJavaScriptEnabled(true) or setAllowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs, so the fail condition is not met.
The single WebView does not enable JavaScript and sets none of the file-access WebSettings. It only renders bundled asset HTML through loadData.
No addJavascriptInterface or @JavascriptInterface in the app sources, and the only WebView does not enable JavaScript.

The sensitive fields (vault password and confirmation, PIN, OTP secret, password dialogs, intro password setup) use textPassword or numberPassword in the layouts or set TYPE_TEXT_VARIATION_PASSWORD in code. Plain text types are only used for non-secret fields such as name, issuer and group.

Password, PIN and secret inputs are masked by default (password input types). setTransformationMethod(null) only runs when the user turns on the 'show password' toggle in Dialogs and SecuritySetupSlide.

Every AegisActivity sets FLAG_SECURE in onCreate when pref_secure_screen is on, which is the default for non-debug builds. Secure dialogs set it too. clearFlags only runs when the user turns the setting off.

The unlock screen and the vault/security settings handle sensitive input. No filterTouchesWhenObscured, onFilterTouchEventForSecurity, FLAG_WINDOW_IS_OBSCURED check or setHideOverlayWindows appears anywhere in sources or layouts.

evidence.detail: Vault password field on the unlock screen has no overlay/tapjacking protection.

fills.reason: The only notification code (NotificationService) never posts its notification: startForeground is commented out, and the service and POST_NOTIFICATIONS are commented out of the manifest. Its text was only the app name and a 'vault unlocked' state, with no OTPs.

Internal navigation uses explicit intents (new Intent(this, X.class)) throughout. Implicit intents are only intentional external delegations: browser/mail in About, gallery/file pickers, SAF documents, date settings, and the user-initiated ACTION_SEND export share.

Sensitive extras (VaultEntry objects) go only into explicit intents to EditEntryActivity and similar. The one implicit intent carrying data is the ACTION_SEND export, a user-chosen share of the export file through the FileProvider.
All three PendingIntent creations use FLAG_IMMUTABLE and explicit base intents (MainActivity.class, or VaultLockReceiver.class with setPackage).
The manifest declares no http/https deep link intent filters. The only VIEW/BROWSABLE filter uses the custom otpauth scheme.

The otpauth handler in MainActivity runs only after the vault is unlocked. It parses the URI with GoogleAuthInfo.parseUri, which checks scheme, secret encoding, type, digits, algorithm and counter, then opens EditEntryActivity so the user confirms before anything is saved.

MainActivity (launcher, otpauth, SEND) handles incoming intents only after the vault is loaded and otherwise starts AuthActivity. PanicResponderActivity is off unless the user enables the panic trigger, and it only acts on intents from senders verified by TrustedIntents signature pins.

The backup rules include shared prefs and backup/aegis.json, a copy of the vault the BackupAgent writes. Cloud backup is skipped unless the user enables it, and that is only possible with an encrypted vault. Device-to-device transfer is allowed regardless, so a vault the user chose not to encrypt is transferred in plaintext. Whether that is acceptable is a product decision.
